title: Counting Advance Days on a Crestline Seat Purchase
content:
**Counting convention — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The advance days of a seat charge are counted by one of three conventions:

| Seat charge | Advance days run |
|---|---|
| Paid online or through the call center within 14 days after the ticket was issued, on a ticket that credits an active Summit membership | From the ticket's issue date to the segment's scheduled departure date |
| Paid at the airport | Zero, whatever the purchase date |
| Any other seat | From the seat's purchase date to the segment's scheduled departure date |

The issue window is 14 days: a seat bought 14 days after issue is within it, one bought 15 days after issue is not. Days are whole calendar days. The seat charge concerned is the latest seat charge recorded for the segment, with the purchase date and channel recorded on it; the membership is the Summit membership the ticket credits.

## Worked cases (hypothetical; ticket issued 1 March, segment departs 20 April)

| Seat purchase | Membership credited | Advance days |
|---|---|---|
| Online, 10 March | Active | 50 (1 March to 20 April) |
| Online, 10 March | None | 41 (10 March to 20 April) |
| Call center, 15 March | Active | 50 (14 days after issue, still within the window) |
| Call center, 16 March | Active | 35 (15 days after issue; counted from purchase) |
| Airport, 20 April | Active | 0 |
